title.narrative: START NETWORK CONFLICT ANTICIPATORY ACTION PROJECT (CAAP)

description.narrative: The project is delivered through a complementary partnership between Christian Aid, the South Sudan Council of Churches (SSCC), and Hope Restoration. Together, they combine technical expertise, faith-based legitimacy and networks deeply rooted in communities across South Sudan. This provides a ready platform to collect, analyse and share timely data for early warning and early action, alongside specialist capacity in conflict prevention/mitigation, protection, and humanitarian response. SSCC is an ecumenical alliance of seven member churches (and several associate churches), established as an independent body in 2011. Building on decades of peacebuilding across the Sudans and membership in the ACT Alliance and Caritas, SSCC is a trusted platform for conflict prevention, early warning/early action, inclusive dialogue, reconciliation, and community engagement. Through its national secretariat in Juba, regional offices, Inter Church Committees (ICCs) and hundreds of local churches, SSCC reaches millions of South Sudanese, including groups often excluded from formal systems. Hope Restoration brings deep humanitarian experience in hard-to-reach, conflict-affected areas of Unity State, Upper Nile and the Equatorias, where access constraints, protection risks and service gaps are most acute. It has operational credibility across sectors—especially protection, peacebuilding, WASH and food security/livelihoods—supporting integrated, context-responsive programming. The organisation has a strong track record on GBV advocacy, protection of civilians and community-based protection, working with local actors to amplify community voices and inform humanitarian and peacebuilding responses, with women, children and other at-risk groups at the centre. Hope Restoration also advances localisation through leadership in national coordination structures and currently chairs the South Sudan Start-up Hub (Start Network), strengthening anticipatory action, early warning analysis and collective advocacy. In this partnership, it bridges community-level intelligence with national synthesis and timely, protection-sensitive, locally led action. Community Early Warning Systems and interface with ICCs: The programme is underpinned by a community-centred early warning system (CEWS) that builds on the reach, legitimacy and convening power of Inter Church Committees (ICCs). ICCs serve as the primary interface between communities and the broader early warning/anticipatory action architecture, ensuring risk analysis reflects lived experience and locally perceived threats
